summary: OpenAI's first in-house inference chip, co-developed with Broadcom. OpenAI has published benchmark results and power figures but not a datasheet: compute layout, memory capacities, process node and interconnect bandwidth are undisclosed. What is known is the design intent — a 'fungible' accelerator that serves both prefill and decode, with model state such as the KV cache explicitly placed and kept local.

p: OpenAI describes chip, memory, network, software and rack as designed together. The network is called integral to the architecture: a large communication domain lets a whole serving workload stay inside one connected system. AI-assisted optimisation of arithmetic circuits was used to pack in more compute.
First results on GPT-OSS 120B, DeepSeek R1 and Kimi K2.5 report 1.5–1.9× more throughput per kilowatt at peak and 1.7–3.6× lower end-to-end latency than the comparison GPU systems.

Core counts and organisation, peak FLOPS, on-chip SRAM capacity, HBM type and capacity, process node, packaging, scale-up topology and bandwidth. The atlas therefore draws no floorplan: the figure below is a disclosure map, not an architecture diagram.

Explicit placement of model state and a balanced prefill/decode design suggest a flexible tensor datapath with software-managed locality. The classification will be revisited once a technical disclosure appears.

c.t: Software + rack co-designed with the chip

caveats: Benchmarks are vendor-published; comparison systems and configurations should be checked in the source before quoting ratios.
Package TDPs cited by OpenAI for comparison GPUs (1,200 W GB200, 1,400 W GB300) are not like-for-like with a 700 W chip rating.
